How They Handle Restricted Countries

When it comes to restricted countries, these platforms typically have a simple solution: they don't serve them. Period. No explanation, no alternatives, just a flat-out rejection. This leaves creators like you high and dry, searching for a solution that doesn't exist. But what if we told you there's a better way? A way that doesn't rely on third-party infrastructure, but instead puts you in control of your digital commerce stack.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

When you use a platform like Lemon Squeezy, you're not just paying for their convenience – you're also paying for the underlying infrastructure costs. Stripe's fees can range from 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction to 0.5% + $0.10 per transaction, depending on your location and payment method. Meanwhile, PayPal's fees can range from 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction to 3.5% + $0.30 per transaction. And let's not forget the hidden costs of account suspensions, which can leave you out of pocket for weeks or even months. With a sovereign commerce infrastructure, you can say goodbye to these unnecessary fees and hello to a more transparent pricing model.
Stripe's geographic exclusion list is a deliberate infrastructure decision — not a temporary gap waiting to be fixed.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

When you build your digital commerce stack on top of a sovereign infrastructure, you own everything. No third-party dependencies, no platform lock-in. You can automate every step of the process, from payment processing to product delivery, without relying on anyone else. And when it comes to delivery, you're not limited to a single provider or method. With a sovereign commerce infrastructure, you have complete control over how your products are delivered to your customers.
